title: The Silent Bell
premise: A harbor apprentice discovers that the city's rescue bell is being silenced before a storm. Her guardian is implicated, but exposing him may leave the harbor without its only trained bell keeper.
reader_experience: Investigation, growing distrust, practical ingenuity, and costly hope
pov: limited third person, Mara, past tense

characters.name: Mara
characters.fear: Remaining dependent on a guardian she cannot fully trust
characters.habitual_strategy: Inspect first, ask guarded questions second

arc.starting_belief: Oren may evade officials but will not mislead her about their shared craft.
arc.old_strategy: Repeat his test and distrust her own result first.
arc.pressure_test: His useful correction is followed by an evasive request for her signature.
arc.costly_choice: Choose whether to stake her own certification or another crew’s equipment on protecting him.
arc.possible_change: Recognize care and coercion in the same relationship without claiming instant independence.

contradiction.conditions: Accuracy is easy to demand until her own signature can protect Oren.

emotional_behavior.under_fear: Checks the same fastening twice and avoids asking the direct question.
emotional_behavior.care: Leaves a tool oriented for the other person’s injured hand.

voice_design.evasion: Asks someone to demonstrate rather than accusing them.
examples: Show me where you took the load off.
I can sign for what I checked. Not for yesterday.

characters.name: Oren
characters.goal: protect Mara and conceal his debt
characters.voice: practical warnings and evasive short answers
characters.fear: Exposure of debt costing his household security
characters.habitual_strategy: Practical help coupled with partial explanations
characters.limits: Cannot operate and repair every station alone

arc.starting_belief: His competence entitles him to manage the truth for people he protects.
arc.old_strategy: Give genuine practical help while withholding the consequential detail.
arc.pressure_test: Mara follows his method and reaches a result he cannot comfortably deny.
arc.costly_choice: Release control of an operation or ask her to become complicit.
arc.possible_change: Accept a limit on authority while remaining defensive about the debt.

contradiction.conditions: Will protect Mara from an immediate injury while putting her professional future at risk.

emotional_behavior.under_fear: Becomes unusually exact about a minor task.
emotional_behavior.under_shame: Repairs something for her instead of apologizing.
emotional_behavior.care: Anticipates a physical difficulty without drawing attention to it.

voice_design.diction: Procedural and economical, with qualifications when cornered.
voice_design.evasion: Answers the safe part of a question and assigns a task.
examples: Hold that end. Then tell me what you think you saw.
I said it would last the watch. I didn’t say it was sound.

characters.name: Ilya
characters.goal: Protect her repair yard and workers
characters.value: Keeping agreements workers can rely on
characters.fear: Losing the yard to council restrictions
characters.proposed_arc: Decide what cooperation is worth risking

arc.starting_belief: A promise that cannot be supplied is worth less than a refusal.
arc.old_strategy: Keep separate commitments separate and price every request.
arc.pressure_test: Mara’s request makes those commitments materially incompatible.
arc.costly_choice: Choose which crew bears the delay and take responsibility for telling them.
arc.possible_change: Negotiate shared liability instead of becoming a convenient helper.

contradiction.conditions: Will bend a council rule but resists asking her own crew to absorb an invisible cost.

emotional_behavior.under_anger: Uses names and delivery times instead of insults.

voice_design.evasion: Insists the requester identify who loses something.
examples: Which crew do you want me to disappoint?
Bring the keeper here. I’m not lending to his apprentice and calling it his promise.

world_rules: The rescue bell requires a physical keeper to sound it.
A storm is expected by the third night.
No magic can restore a severed rope.

initial_facts.text: Oren trained Mara to inspect the bell mechanism.
Oren owes a private debt to the harbor collector.
Ilya knows the yard’s available supplies and council restrictions.
The bell tower, repair yard, council office, and docks are within a working harbor.

must_avoid: Instant reconciliation without a consequential choice
main_plot: Discover how and why the bell was disabled, then make a consequential decision before the storm arrives.
subplots: Mara’s dependence on Oren affects what she investigates and risks.
Ilya’s threatened livelihood affects the materials and cooperation available for rescue.
scene_requirements: A failed attempt to obtain help
reference_policy: Combine mechanisms across sources; invent original circumstances and preserve causal function. Do not copy plots.
creative_freedom: May invent minor complications; keep the supplied cast IDs and explicit facts, no new major characters.
surprise: moderate; established possibilities must support surprises
sensory_detail: moderate; details affect work, danger, or viewpoint attention
ending_tendency: Resolve the bell crisis, preserve personal cost, allow incomplete reconciliation.

scene_designs.setting: Morning light, harbor crews below, a scheduled load test rather than a generic stormy room
scene_designs.dramatic_function: A familiar shared task reveals a discrepancy that Oren initially helps investigate. Establish reciprocal competence before distrust.
sensory_actions: A chalk mark moves when the brake slips.
Old grease transfers to the wrong tool.
constraints: Do not identify an obvious sabotage device immediately.
End with an action or changed obligation, not an announced moral dilemma.

scene_designs.location: tower service landing and maintenance desk
scene_designs.setting: An inspection signature is due while crews need the lifting line
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Mara tries to protect both the harbor and Oren. Her workaround creates a new cost or complicity; she does not rediscover that he lied.
constraints: Test the obvious option of repairing quietly.
Make the availability of reporting, concealing, and repairing concrete.

scene_designs.setting: Ilya has workers and an unfinished boat demanding the same limited equipment
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Mara’s chosen workaround intersects Ilya’s independent livelihood problem and changes what both can do.

world_design.technology: Mechanical maritime infrastructure: rope, brake, bell, hand tools, oil lamps. No electrical switches or magic resolving mechanical faults.

institutions.authority: Schedules shared equipment and records inspections.
institutions.constraints: A fault report suspends the keeper’s certification pending inspection; it does not automatically evict an apprentice.
institutions.cost: Suspension removes Oren from an essential shift and delays Mara’s qualification.

physical_systems.purpose: Warn approaching crews to turn toward the marked safe channel during poor visibility.
operation: A keeper releases the brake and works the counterweighted rope.
The brake and the channel-watch signal are distinct from the bell’s clapper.
failure_modes: Rope wear can leave the bell operable but unsafe for sustained ringing.
A temporary brace may conceal a worn brake; diagnosis requires an unloaded test.
alternatives: A watch boat can carry the warning, but reallocating it leaves a crew without an escort.
limits: Do not invent new gears as convenient solutions.
Removing one obstruction does not automatically repair worn components.

deadlines.change_policy: An earlier arrival needs an observed warning, an explicit revised time, and consequences reflected in later scene cards.

economic_dependencies: Mara needs Oren’s assessed practical hours for certification.
Ilya controls a scarce replacement part already promised to a working crew.

plot_design.central_question: What does Mara owe a guardian whose protection is becoming a demand for complicity?
causal_dependencies: Establish a legitimate mechanical danger before Oren uses it to justify concealment.
Mara’s attempt to repair quietly creates a documented cost.
That cost intersects Ilya’s independent obligation.
The ending uses a capacity or agreement established through earlier choices.

subplots.question: Will Mara accept competence that depends on Oren’s approval?
subplots.intersection: Her attempt to act independently risks the assessed hours needed for qualification.
subplots.removal_cost: Without this thread, her reliance on him is merely narrated.

subplots.question: Which commitment will Ilya break when two crews require the same equipment?
subplots.intersection: Mara’s rescue plan demands the part Ilya already promised elsewhere.
subplots.removal_cost: Without this thread, Ilya becomes a supply dispenser serving the protagonist.

alternatives_and_costs.cost: Needs scarce equipment and an inaccurate inspection entry; test whether Mara will actually sign it.
A suspended keeper and interrupted work before another operator is available; no invented automatic homelessness.
Takes protection from a specific crew with whom Ilya has an obligation.

resolution_constraints: A successful warning does not erase the broken inspection promise.
Forgiveness, professional trust, and personal loyalty may end in different states.

references.purpose: Conflicting obligations with genuine counterarguments; do not borrow the burial plot or require tragedy.
A private decision changes what a working community can safely do.
Rescue or protection creates incompatible debts rather than an automatic obligation to obey.

adaptation.policy: Use a small mechanism or relationship move; do not force reference material into every scene or treat adaptation strength as a measured similarity percentage.

style.interiority: Add a competing interpretation, mistaken inference, or tactical decision; omit explanation of an already legible gesture.
style.dialogue: Each speaker pursues a different immediate objective. They need not answer the question asked.
style.explanation: Trust the reader; do not restate the theme or dilemma at scene endings.
style.rhythm: Follow pressure and thought rather than automatic triplets or not-X-but-Y pivots.

length_policy.policy: 850 words is a planning estimate. Expand through action, negotiation, and consequences; never pad a repeated discovery to reach a minimum.
